findings.evidence: renovate/default.json root-level: `"labels": ["dependencies", "scp-federation"]` — applied to all PRs from this preset; renovate/default.json packageRule for jrnb2024/standards-control-plane: `"labels": ["dependencies", "scp-federation", "scp-bump"]` — `scp-bump` is the discriminating label for SCP primitive bump PRs only; ADOPT-001 §12.7.5 step 0: 'Close any open Renovate-bot PR that is bumping the wrapper SHA pin (label: `scp-federation` per the preset's packageRules).'
findings.impact: During an SCP regression rollback, an operator following the documented step 0 closes every Renovate PR in their repo labeled `scp-federation`, which — given the root-level label — includes all Renovate-managed dependency updates (npm, pip, go.mod, etc.) that the adopter's Renovate instance generates while extending this preset. This (a) interrupts legitimate dependency updates with no relation to the SCP regression, (b) potentially delays security patches on unrelated dependencies whose Renovate PRs were just closed, and (c) could trigger Renovate rate-limiting on PR recreation. The root label was present at v1.0.0 and the discrepancy was not caught in R1 or R2.
findings.mitigation: Replace 'label: `scp-federation`' in §12.7.5 step 0 with 'label: `scp-bump`', which is the packageRule-specific label exclusive to SCP federation primitive bump PRs. The corrected step 0 becomes: 'Close any open Renovate-bot PR that is bumping the wrapper SHA pin (label: `scp-bump` per the preset's SCP-primitive packageRule; this is distinct from the root-level `scp-federation` label, which appears on all Renovate PRs from this preset).' This scopes the rollback closure to exactly the PR series that poses the risk without disturbing unrelated dependency updates.

findings.claim: The R2 SAFE-R2-001 MAJ finding's mitigation explicitly requested TWO changes: (1) text in §12.7.4 requiring dismiss_stale_reviews: true (implemented); and (2) a WARNING in enable-required-check.sh when the preserved existing review config has dismiss_stale_reviews=false or null (NOT implemented). The FIX-ROUND-3 record describes the closure as text-only: 'The enable-required-check.sh helper preserves existing review-shape verbatim and does not set this for adopters; the appendix instructs explicit configuration via the GitHub UI/API.' The helper script at line 311 silently preserves whatever review config it finds (`EXISTING_REVIEWS="$(printf '%s' "$BEFORE_JSON" | jq '.required_pull_request_reviews // null')"`), without any check on the dismiss_stale_reviews field value.
findings.evidence: enable-required-check.sh line 311: `EXISTING_REVIEWS="$(printf '%s' "$BEFORE_JSON" | jq '.required_pull_request_reviews // null')"` — no subsequent check on `.dismiss_stale_reviews // false` value and no conditional WARNING emit; FIX-ROUND-3.md SAFE-R2-001 closure: 'The enable-required-check.sh helper preserves existing review-shape verbatim and does not set this for adopters; the appendix instructs explicit configuration via the GitHub UI/API' — no mention of implementing the helper warning; review-safety-r2.json SAFE-R2-001 mitigation part (2): 'Add to enable-required-check.sh: when extracting $existing_reviews, check whether dismiss_stale_reviews is false (or null) and emit a WARNING if so, recommending the adopter set it to true before proceeding.'
findings.impact: A multi-maintainer adopter who runs the helper on a repo with dismiss_stale_reviews=false (or on a fresh repo with null review config, which the helper preserves as null/no-reviews) receives no signal from the tool itself. The attacker scenario from SAFE-R2-001 partially remains: an adopter who configures branch protection via the helper and then OMITS the follow-up UI step to set dismiss_stale_reviews=true has Gate 1 partially open — a contributor could obtain a CODEOWNER review on an initial commit then push bypass-surface content after approval without triggering re-review. The §12.7.4 text-only mitigation relies entirely on the adopter reading the appendix prior to running the helper; operators who run the helper first and read the docs later (a common pattern) receive no tool-level protection signal.
findings.mitigation: Add a dismiss_stale_reviews warning to enable-required-check.sh immediately after line 311 where EXISTING_REVIEWS is extracted: `dismiss_stale_val="$(printf '%s' "$EXISTING_REVIEWS" | jq -r '.dismiss_stale_reviews // false')"; if [ "$dismiss_stale_val" != 'true' ]; then echo 'WARNING: your current required_pull_request_reviews does not have dismiss_stale_reviews: true. For multi-maintainer SCP adoption, dismiss_stale_reviews: true is required (see ADOPT-001 §12.7.4). Configure it explicitly via the GitHub branch-protection UI or API after this script completes.' >&2; fi`. The text disclosure in §12.7.4 remains the normative requirement; the helper warning provides the defence-in-depth layer the R2 mitigation originally specified but which was not implemented in fix-round-3.

findings.claim: The 2026-05-14 closure deadline for TF-020H3-001 (Regal SHA256 supply-chain gap) is recorded in STATUS.md's 'Tracked-forward items from 020H part 3' section but is ABSENT from the 'Open scheduled follow-ups' table. The follow-ups table is the primary operator surface for time-sensitive action items — all five current entries have explicit calendar dates and sources. TF-020H3-001's 2026-05-14 deadline is NOT in that table. An operator who scans the follow-ups table for near-term deadlines (a reasonable operational habit given the table's design) would not see the 2026-05-14 date, reducing the deadline to an item that relies on the operator's memory of the tracked-forward section rather than the time-sensitive prompt the table provides.
findings.evidence: STATUS.md 'Open scheduled follow-ups' table: five entries (D-021 on 2026-05-31, Phase 2 notice on 2026-07-02, bearer-legacy close on 2026-09-30, quarterly review on 2026-07-21, branch-protection review on 2026-07-30) — no TF-020H3-001 entry; STATUS.md 'Tracked-forward items from 020H part 3': 'TF-020H3-001: ... Closure deadline: 2026-05-14 (14 days from 020H part 3 merge) OR before v1.0.1 release, whichever comes first. Escalate to user review if deferred beyond this window.' — correct deadline present but not in follow-ups table; DISPATCH-NOTE.md TF-020H3-001: 'Closure deadline: before v1.0.1 release OR within 14 calendar days of 020H part 3 merge (whichever comes first); for a 2026-04-30 merge, that is 2026-05-14.' The R2 finding SAFE-R2-004 explicitly requested this concrete deadline, and the deadline WAS added — but only to the tracked-forward section, not the follow-ups table.
findings.mitigation: Add a row to STATUS.md 'Open scheduled follow-ups' table: `| TF-020H3-001 Regal SHA256 gap → slice 020H.2 (Regal SHA256 verification) | 2026-05-14 | docs/reviews/WP-SCP-022/dispatches/020h3/DISPATCH-NOTE.md TF-020H3-001 + ADOPT-001 §12.7.13 |`. This surfaces the deadline in the operator's primary time-sensitive tracking surface alongside the other dated items, removing the reliance on memory of the tracked-forward section. The 2026-05-14 deadline is the more urgent of the two conditions (14 days from merge vs before v1.0.1 release, whichever is first); the table entry should reflect the concrete date.

findings.claim: §12.7.4's explanation of dismiss_stale_reviews says 'without it, an approving CODEOWNER review on an initial commit persists across subsequent commits in the same PR.' This is accurate but does not explicitly confirm that dismiss_stale_reviews fires on ALL pushes to the PR branch regardless of which paths are changed — including pushes that touch only non-CODEOWNERS paths. An adopter might reasonably wonder whether a new commit that touches only a file not in CODEOWNERS (e.g., a source code file) still triggers stale-review dismissal, or whether the dismissal is path-selective. The current text implies path-agnostic dismissal but does not state it.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.4: 'The dismiss_stale_reviews: true setting is non-optional in this mode: without it, an approving CODEOWNER review on an initial commit persists across subsequent commits in the same PR, so an attacker who obtains a clean review can later push commits that add .scp/rule-config.yaml disable: true, change scp_bypass: true, or weaken the wrapper's fork-PR if: — and merge without re-review.'; GitHub branch-protection documentation: dismiss_stale_reviews fires when 'someone pushes a new commit' — the dismissal is a per-PR-branch event, not a per-path event; it fires regardless of which files the new commit changes.
findings.mitigation: Add one clause to §12.7.4's dismiss_stale_reviews description: 'Dismissal fires on ANY push to the PR branch regardless of which files the new commit touches — it is not path-selective.' This preempts the reasonable adopter question and confirms the control is stronger than a path-scoped protection.

structured_review.summary: APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS — fixpoint criterion met: zero new CRIT or MAJ findings across a comprehensive adversarial re-examination of all six dispatch question axes. All R1 MAJ closures (SAFE-003: two-mode single/multi breakdown; SAFE-009: rule-config bypass disclosure; SAFE-011: Regal ACE disclosure with TF-020H3-001) verified genuine at post-fix-round-4 state. All R2 closures verified genuine: SAFE-R2-001 (dismiss_stale_reviews: text requirement added, helper limitation disclosed); SAFE-R2-002 (§11.10 upgraded to normative MUST); SAFE-R2-003 (§12.7.1 + §12.7.9 forward-references to §12.7.13 present); SAFE-R2-004 (concrete 2026-05-14 deadline added to DISPATCH-NOTE and STATUS.md tracked-forward section); SAFE-R2-005 (D-031 item (c) has D-033 amendment annotation). The dismiss_stale_reviews closure (SAFE-R2-001) is robust for the 'review-then-push-malicious-commit' attack: GitHub dismisses ALL reviews on ANY push to the PR branch regardless of which paths are touched, so the path-agnostic property holds. The non-author platform enforcement claim is accurate for all merge types (squash, rebase, merge commit). The de-adoption Case A contexts:[] correctly removes the SCP-only required check; Case B stale-context risk is operational (over-blocking) not a privilege leak. Cross-document consistency (ADOPT-001 §12.7 / DECISIONS.md / STATUS.md / docs/security/branch-protection.md) verified: all four agree on single-operator live state (count=0, codeowner=false, dismiss_stale=true, enforce_admins=true, policy-check/scp/policy-check context). Four MIN residuals surface: (1) SAFE-R3-001: §12.7.4 Gate 1 'typically' wording could lead an adopter to protect services.yml only, leaving waivers.json uncovered and Gate 1 potentially non-CODEOWNER-specific on bypass PRs; (2) SAFE-R3-002: §12.7.5 step 0 rollback label uses scp-federation (root-level — all Renovate PRs) instead of scp-bump (SCP-primitive-specific) — operational footgun during rollback; (3) SAFE-R3-003: enable-required-check.sh does not warn when preserved dismiss_stale_reviews is false/null — R2 mitigation component explicitly requested but not implemented; (4) SAFE-R3-004: TF-020H3-001's 2026-05-14 deadline is absent from STATUS.md 'Open scheduled follow-ups' table, leaving it outside the primary operator time-sensitive tracking surface. One nit (SAFE-R3-005): dismiss_stale_reviews description doesn't confirm the dismissal is push-type-agnostic. No findings recommend descoping. All mitigations are additive text or script changes.
